title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.81): P_1 is an additive ⊗-category (Grothendieck allows √, possibly meaning Karoubian). It carries a 'divided power' structure Γ^* : (P_1,⊕) → (graded objects of P_1, ⊗). The data are:
- Γ^0 = 1 and Γ^1 = id;
- an exponential isomorphism Γ^*(X⊕Y) ≅ Γ^*X ⊗ Γ^*Y, with Γ^*(0) = 1;
- natural maps α_{p,q} : Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q, subject to an associativity condition;
- normalisations α_{1,q} = α_{q,1} = id and α_{0,q} = id, with α_{q,0} : Γ^0 = 1 → Γ^q(Γ^0) = Γ^q(1).

On this page he uses these data to build a category whose morphisms carry a degree. Define P_p(X,Y) := Hom(Γ^p X, Y), the 'morphisms homogeneous of degree p'. Then P_1(X,Y) = Hom_{P_1}(X,Y), and P_0(X,Y) = Hom(1,Y) are the 'constants'.

Composition P_p(X,Y) × P_q(Y,Z) → P_{pq}(X,Z) is defined by
  g∘f = g ∘ Γ^q(f) ∘ α^X_{q,p} : Γ^{pq}X → Γ^qΓ^pX → Γ^qY → Z.

The model is Roby's description of homogeneous polynomial laws: degree-p polynomial maps M → N are the same as linear maps Γ^pM → N. In that model, α_{q,p} : Γ^{pq}M → Γ^qΓ^pM is the linear map classifying the degree-pq polynomial map x ↦ γ_q(γ_p(x)), which is dual to the plethysm S^q S^p → S^{pq}.

The page then checks the axioms:
- Associativity of composition follows from the associativity condition on α.
- The case p = q = 1 reduces to ordinary composition, i.e. to the bifunctoriality of P_p(X,Y) on P_1^op × P_1.
- The unit compatibilities (axiom 2) give g∘f = g when g has degree 0: a constant composed after anything is that constant.
- Composing g with a constant f : 1 → Y requires the map α_{q,0} : 1 → Γ^q(1), i.e. γ_q(1) = 1.

Grothendieck notes he had forgotten this last map in the 'preliminary axioms'. The next page uses the exponential isomorphism to obtain multi-degree morphisms P_{ν_1..ν_r}(X_1..X_r; Y). It then defines 'strict polynomial categories' and '⊗-pd-categories' and says the two notions are essentially equivalent.

Purpose within cote 137: to axiomatise divided-power / polynomial structures, as on perfect complexes and K-theory with Γ^n or λ-operations. This would allow dévissage arguments for multiplicative structures to be carried out in an abstract 'polynomial category'.

In modern terms, (Γ^p, α_{p,q}, Γ^1 = id) is a comonad graded by the multiplicative monoid (N, ·, 1), and P_• is its graded co-Kleisli category. The exponential law Γ^*(X⊕Y) ≅ Γ^*X ⊗ Γ^*Y is a Seely-type isomorphism.
errors: Gap acknowledged by Grothendieck himself: composing with degree-0 morphisms (constants) needs the structure map α_{q,0} : 1 → Γ^q(1), plus compatibility conditions for it. He says he forgot it in the preliminary axioms. On p.81 it appears only as 'unique[?]' without justification.

Indexing convention: the composition uses α_{q,p} : Γ^{pq} → Γ^q∘Γ^p, with the outer functor indexed by the degree of g. This is consistent, but the associativity axiom must be stated with this order for associativity of composition to follow. This is not written out explicitly here.
Only the unit compatibilities are sketched. Compatibility of composition with the additive structure is not addressed on this page; composition is not bilinear in f, since Γ^q(f) is polynomial in f.

ideas.what: Morphisms of degree p defined as P_p(X,Y) = Hom(Γ^p X, Y), modelling homogeneous polynomial maps of degree p through divided powers
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of divided powers for polynomial laws; strict polynomial maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963) for polynomial laws and Γ; Friedlander–Suslin (1997) for strict polynomial functors

ideas.what: Composition P_p × P_q → P_{pq} via the natural plethysm maps α_{q,p} : Γ^{pq} → Γ^qΓ^p, with the axioms Γ^1 = id, α_{1,q} = α_{q,1} = id, and associativity
ideas.modern_name: Graded comonad indexed by the monoid (N,·) and its graded co-Kleisli category

ideas.what: Degree-0 morphisms as constants Hom(1,Y), with the unit map 1 → Γ^q(1) (γ_q(1) = 1)
ideas.modern_name: Unit compatibility for graded comonad / divided power structure

ideas.what: Abstract '⊗-pd-category' / 'strict polynomial category': an additive ⊗-category with Γ^n satisfying the exponential law and plethysm maps (defined on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Category with divided power structure; relates to strict polynomial functor categories and exponential modalities
ideas.usually_credited_to: Friedlander–Suslin, Touzé, Krause (polynomial functors); Seely/Girard (exponential modality)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly builds the co-Kleisli category of a comonad graded by the multiplicative monoid (N,·,1): Γ^p is the graded comonad, α_{q,p} its comultiplication, Γ^1 = id its counit, and morphism sets P_p(X,Y) = Hom(Γ^p X, Y) compose with degrees multiplying. This is the structure later studied as graded monads/comonads and their (co)Kleisli categories, here motivated by divided powers in algebraic K-theory.
missed.quote: P_p(X,Y)×P_q(Y,Z) → P_{pq}(X,Z) ... g∘f = g Γ^q(f) α^X_{q,p}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an early, algebraic-geometric instance of graded co-Kleisli categories, predating the computer-science literature by ~30 years. It ties polynomial-functor theory (Friedlander–Suslin, Touzé) to graded-comonad formalism.

missed.claim: Together with p.81's exponential law Γ^*(X⊕Y) ≅ Γ^*X ⊗ Γ^*Y and Γ^*(0) = 1, the structure is a degree-graded exponential modality satisfying Seely isomorphisms. This is essentially a model of bounded/graded linear logic in which divided powers replace symmetric powers, the natural choice in positive characteristic.
missed.quote: Γ^*(X⊕Y)≃Γ^*(X)⊗Γ^*(Y) (iso gr. ann., fonctoriel...) ; Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Divided-power models of exponentials and of differential linear logic are a current topic. Grothendieck's axiomatics, including 'strict polynomial category' vs '⊗-pd-category', anticipate them.

missed.claim: The axiomatic notion of a '(strict) polynomial category' / '⊗-pd-category' as a general framework for dévissage of multiplicative (λ/Γ) structures on perfect complexes appears to be left in sketch form, including the missing axiom on α_{q,0}.
missed.quote: Je l'avais oublié dans les axiomes préliminaires
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean axiomatics of categories with divided-power plethysm could serve derived/animated divided powers and λ-structures on K-theory. This is an active area, e.g. derived binomial rings and derived λ-rings.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction itself (polynomial maps via Γ^p, composing with degrees multiplying) is natural for a specialist in divided powers. However, the explicit axiomatisation as a graded co-Kleisli category with Seely-type exponential law, in the service of K-theoretic dévissage, appears unpublished. It anticipates later graded-monad and polynomial-category formalisms.
transcription_corrections: 'pour la dimension[?]' and 'la dimension[?] signifie' are more plausibly 'pour la dernière/deuxième' and 'la deuxième signifie', referring to the two compatibility conditions (**) and (***) from p.81.
'α_{q,0}' in the circled formula is the map 1 → Γ^q(1); the crossed-out symbol above it seems to be an abandoned index label.
'Diph[?]' in the crossed-out opening line is probably the start of a word like 'Diff…' or 'D…'; the whole line is struck out.
In the composition diagram the struck-out middle term was replaced by Γ^q(f) : Γ^qΓ^pX → Γ^qY, followed by g : Γ^qY → Z.
